claim_text: The evaluation uses a synthetic CCTNS/ICJS-style inter-agency access-governance workload, not real police records.
safe_wording: We evaluate SEBA-XAI on a synthetic inter-agency access-request workload inspired by CCTNS/ICJS-style sharing.
limitations: Does not prove real CCTNS/ICJS performance or access to real police records.

claim_text: SEBA-XAI is an access-governance and audit paper, not a crime-prediction paper.
safe_wording: The paper studies access governance, auditability, and explanation of access decisions rather than individual crime prediction.
limitations: NCRB/BPRD can be used for context only unless separate aggregate modeling is implemented.

claim_text: The prototype compares mutable logs, signed hash chains, blockchain-style audit, CT-style logs, ABAC/Fabric-style re-execution, trusted policy oracle, and NS-PI.
safe_wording: We compare multiple audit and policy-checking baselines under explicit visibility assumptions.
limitations: Some baselines are simulations, not deployed production systems.

claim_text: The blockchain component is a permissioned blockchain-style audit simulation.
safe_wording: The blockchain layer is a local permissioned-audit simulation that records commitments and detects controlled tampering.
limitations: No real Hyperledger Fabric test-network evidence exists yet.

claim_text: Mutable logs are weak for controlled tamper cases.
safe_wording: The mutable log baseline does not internally detect the controlled edits in the local tamper test.
limitations: This is based on the implemented mutable-log baseline, not all possible database audit systems.

claim_text: Signed hash-chain logs detect the controlled edits in the local tamper test.
safe_wording: The signed hash-chain baseline detects the controlled edits in the local test.
limitations: Does not prevent validly re-signed compromised events.

claim_text: Blockchain-style audit detects controlled block and commitment edits.
safe_wording: The permissioned blockchain-style blocks detect the controlled block and commitment edits in the local simulation.
limitations: No live Fabric deployment; does not imply production security.

claim_text: Cryptographic and ABAC-style defenses remain stronger than mutable logs for ordinary event edits in the tested workload.
safe_wording: For ordinary event edits, cryptographic and ABAC-style defenses perform better than the mutable log baseline in the synthetic benchmark.
metric_or_row_filter: ordinary attacks excluding compromised_signer; AAS values
limitations: Should not be generalized beyond the implemented attack catalog.

claim_text: Trusted policy oracle has the highest overall AAS in the current synthetic benchmark.
safe_wording: The trusted policy oracle reaches the strongest overall result under its independent raw-attribute visibility assumption.
limitations: Strong assumption; not a free operational guarantee.

claim_text: NS-PI is not the strongest overall detector.
safe_wording: NS-PI is not the best overall tamper detector; it is a complementary log-only drift signal.
limitations: Do not claim NS-PI beats blockchain, ABAC, or trusted policy oracle overall.

claim_text: Ledger-only and ABAC/Fabric-style checks are blind to the validly re-signed compromised-signer attack as implemented.
safe_wording: For the synthetic compromised-signer attack, ledger-only and ABAC-style baselines have 0.0 detection because the corrupted log is validly re-signed by construction.
limitations: Attack realism must be explained carefully; not all real attacks follow this pattern.

claim_text: NS-PI detects the full-grid compromised-signer attack in the five-seed setting.
safe_wording: NS-PI detects the tested validly re-signed compromised-signer attack in the full-grid five-seed setting.
limitations: Does not hold for all flip rates or targeted attacks.

claim_text: Trusted policy oracle also detects the compromised-signer attack.
safe_wording: The trusted policy oracle also detects the compromised-signer attack because it re-evaluates against an independent raw-attribute view.
limitations: Requires uncompromised original request attributes.

claim_text: NS-PI misses 2% and 5% global compromised-signer corruption.
safe_wording: NS-PI misses 2% and 5% global corruption in the current synthetic sensitivity study.
limitations: Detection boundary is workload-dependent.

claim_text: NS-PI detects global compromised-signer corruption from 10% in the current workload, with size caveats.
safe_wording: In the current sensitivity study, NS-PI detects the global compromised-signer attack from 10%, but stress results show this threshold is workload-size dependent.
limitations: At N=500, 10% detection is not stable; do not state a universal threshold.

claim_text: Global NS-PI is weak for localized station/district attacks.
safe_wording: Global NS-PI is weak for localized attacks because the changed share of the full workload can remain small.
metric_or_row_filter: target_scope station/district; low global detection rates
limitations: Grouped drift is needed for this threat model.

claim_text: Grouped NS-PI helps for targeted corruption but misses small target-group corruption.
safe_wording: Grouped NS-PI improves targeted attack detection but still misses 10% target-group corruption in the current benchmark.
metric_or_row_filter: target flip 0.10 any detection=0.0; higher flips improved
limitations: Not a row-level verifier; targeted sensitivity depends on group size.

claim_text: XAI traces are complete in the current synthetic evaluation.
safe_wording: The structured XAI trace is complete across the five-seed synthetic evaluation.
limitations: Completeness of generated traces does not prove human usefulness.

claim_text: Counterfactual explanations are generated for all current deny/escalate target rows.
safe_wording: Counterfactual coverage is complete in the current workload.
limitations: Generated counterfactuals still need human/domain validation for real use.

claim_text: Counterfactual validity is high but not perfect.
safe_wording: Counterfactual validity is high in the current benchmark, with a measured mean of 0.9964.
limitations: Do not round into perfection; report the measured non-perfect value.

claim_text: Natural-language explanation text does not mention every decisive attribute in all cases.
safe_wording: Decisive-attribute full text coverage is incomplete and should be reported as an explanation-quality limitation.
limitations: This is a weakness unless renderer is improved and rerun.

claim_text: Audit reconstruction succeeds in the current synthetic benchmark.
safe_wording: Audit reconstruction succeeds across the tested events by joining request records, signed-chain events, block index rows, and block commitments.
limitations: Does not prove production audit reconstruction in CCTNS/ICJS.

claim_text: Minimized commitment ledger reduces schema-level metadata exposure in the synthetic study.
safe_wording: The minimized commitment ledger reduces the prototype schema-level exposure score compared with full metadata logging.
limitations: This is not a formal privacy proof and does not measure every side channel.

claim_text: Local latency and storage overhead have been measured for the prototype components.
safe_wording: The paper can report local prototype latency and storage measurements for policy oracle, mutable log, signed hash chain, and permissioned blockchain-style audit.
limitations: Local timings are not production CCTNS/ICJS or Fabric performance.

claim_text: Removing policy rule groups changes false-allow/escalation behavior.
safe_wording: Policy ablation shows why contextual rules matter, especially privacy, sealed-record, sensitivity, and jurisdiction checks.
limitations: Ablation reflects the synthetic policy design, not official policy.

claim_text: Blockchain alone is insufficient for this research problem.
safe_wording: Blockchain-style audit helps with tamper-evident commitments, but it does not decide whether a validly signed access decision was policy-correct.
limitations: Must distinguish ledger integrity from policy correctness.

claim_text: ABAC/PBAC is central, not optional decoration.
safe_wording: Contextual access policy is central because RBAC-only rules produce many false allows in the synthetic workload.
limitations: Do not claim exact real-world false-allow rates.

claim_text: XAI is used for audit review, not to make the system automatically trustworthy.
safe_wording: XAI artifacts support reviewability by logging decision traces, reason codes, decisive attributes, counterfactuals, and hashes.
limitations: No human-subject review study has been conducted.

claim_text: The current paper is not a live deployment, real police data, formal cryptography, formal privacy, or production Fabric paper.
safe_wording: The current evidence supports a synthetic benchmark and prototype paper only.
limitations: Keep this limitation visible in abstract, methodology, and limitations.

claim_text: Stronger claims require reproduction freeze, artifact-to-claim completion, optional real Fabric validation, and possible explanation renderer improvement.
safe_wording: Before stronger claims, run the reproduction freeze, complete final claim audit, and either improve explanation text coverage or retain the limitation.
limitations: These are planned next steps, not completed new results.
